pr_title: drivers: display: st7789v: implement display_set_orientation API
pr_body:
Add support for 135x240, 240x320, 240x240 displays at 0, 90, 180, and 270 degree orientation.

closes #32286
pr_comments:
Hello @LuskeyNoah, I'm also working on a similar PR for the ssd16xx driver (but focusing on setting the orientation in the DTS first in combination with correct LVGL init). I'm curious why you chose not to switch x/y_resolution in the get_capabilities function, wich is done here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/display/display_ili9xxx.c#L246.

I was traveling the ili9xxx road and got into an issue by switching those parameters in the get_capabilities function. LVGL init fails because this bit of glue code here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/modules/lvgl/lvgl.c#L107. The allocation function assumes X matches the display width and Y matches the the display height, which is not the case anymore when the display driver already has them switched. As a result, the lvgl_init fails for non-square resolutions.

I decided that the driver does not need to switch the resolutions (like with your implementation), but then LVGL needs to do it, so I think the glue code needs a "disp_drv.rotated = ..." (in lvgl_init()) based on the current orientation from the display capabilities. This is what I'm going for at the moment but I wonder if touching the glue code like that will break other display orientation implementations.

Also, based on my findings I actually think that ili9xxx + lvgl sample does not work currently when the orientation is 90/270 degrees (as initial orientation, using dts), but I cannot verify because I lack the necessary HW to test.

What are your thoughts on this?

>  I'm curious why you chose not to switch x/y_resolution in the get_capabilities function, wich is done here

@Snevzor - good catch. This is an oversight on my part. I'm pushing an update, as it looks like [other drivers](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/598ab6b39a5e38466a286fb317f39bcd34b8ad20/drivers/display/display_gc9x01x.c#L636) choose to take the approach of reporting the swapped dimensions.
@LuskeyNoah I'm still a bit confused about the correct approach on this. Please refer to my comment here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/73360#issuecomment-2143410580.
I do not have the proper hardware to confidently/fully test this. Closing. @Snevzor please reopen and/or contribute to it if desired. I will reopen if I can fully test this.
@LuskeyNoah I unfortunately also do not have a st7789 based display laying around, I'm sorry.

Hi @DBS06,

For this to work well with LVGL this is needed: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/73556.
Also, in context to why this PR was abandoned, https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/82582 needs to be clarified fist. --> for this PR I think your best bet is to make sure the driver doesn't switch x/y resolution and then to test with the changes from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/73556.

Maybe check with @danieldegrasse?

Br,
Sven
@Snevzor Thanks for the fast response and clarification!

issue_context.title: ST7789 driver enhancement to support display orientation
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Unable to change the ST7789 display orientation. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The ability to set the ST7789 display orientation through st7789v_set_orientation(). The function exists
for driver but it is not implemented currently.

In reviewing the drivers for the other popular displays, like the ILI9340, it appears the display orientation function for those displays have not been implemented either. 

Is the absence of the display orientation due to the level of implementation difficulty or  just a lower priority? 
It certainly would be a very useful feature. 
I suspect if and when the functionality gets added, it'll be there for all the Zephyr supported display drivers.
 
Display orientation for the above displays is available under other frameworks/platforms, for example Arduino, Adafruit, and other ESP32/STM32 display drivers.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I have looked into seeing if the LVGL graphics library could somehow be used. They recommend that the functionality be handled by the display driver.  

**Additional context**
Add any other context or graphics (drag-and-drop an image) about the feature request here.
comments: @vanwinkeljan Let me know if you need any assistance in testing out the ST7789 display orientation functionality once you’ve added the support. From the self-assignment, I assume you’ll be adding the set orientation function for the SAt7789 display controller. Thanks.
@vanwinkeljan, Any progress on the ST7789 display orientation support? Thanks.

@key1066 sorry no progress on this. I currently have not the time or the HW to look into this.

As you have the HW feel free to send a PR introducing orientation support.

> 

Can you help with testing?
I checked on two displays st7789
240×320 and 240×135
https://www.waveshare.com/product/displays/lcd-oled/lcd-oled-3/2inch-lcd-module.htm
https://www.waveshare.com/product/displays/lcd-oled/lcd-oled-3/1.14inch-lcd-module.htm

What displays can you check?

Hi! 
I have several ST7789 displays from Waveshare (240x240 1.3”, 240x320 2.4” and 2”, and 240x135 1.14”) and generic 240x240 1.3” without CS. 
I’d be glad to test these out with the ST7789 driver updates. Let me know when the code is ready for testing. Thanks.

@cvetaevvitaliy, I've tested the updated driver with the following five ST7789 displays: 

- Waveshare 135x240 Pico-LCD-1.14"
https://www.waveshare.com/pico-lcd-1.14.htm

- Generic 135x240 1.14"
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/4000571253836.html?spm=a2g0o.store_pc_allProduct.8148356.2.76ef4de3OsXkJN

- Waveshare 320x240, 2" LCD Display Module For Raspberry Pi Pico
https://www.waveshare.com/pico-lcd-2.htm

- Waveshare 240x240, 1.3" IPS LCD Display HAT For Raspberry Pi
https://www.waveshare.com/product/raspberry-pi/displays/lcd-oled/1.3inch-lcd-hat.htm

- Waveshare 240x240, 1.3" LCD Display Module For Raspberry Pi Pico
https://www.waveshare.com/pico-lcd-1.14.htm

Results:
I'm using ST7789 with LVGL under Zephyr 2.70 on a micro:bit v2 with the same code for all tests except changing the st7789 width/height in the microbit_v2_overlay for the display under test.

1. The updated drivers works fine for all rotations (0,90,180, and 270) for the 135x240 and 320x240 displays.
2. Mixed results for Waveshare 240x240 displays. 
microbit_v2_overlay: width = height = 240, x-offset = y-offset = 0
Rotations 0 & 270 degrees work fine.
Rotations of 90 & 180 have display area shifted off the display by 80 but rotation direction is correct. Setting y-offset = 80 corrects the shift but introduces shift off the display for rotations of 0 and 270 degrees. 

I'll investigate further under debug but expected the rotations to work correctly with 240x240 display overlay settings above.
